title: Extension of residue cycle comparisons to product terms
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, kappa an R-algebra which is a field, V and M_i R-modules, H_i additive groups, and P_i parameter types. Let Z_i be kappa-subspaces of kappa tensor M_i and beta_i additive maps from Z_i to H_i. Suppose every admissible b_i(phi): V to M_i sends each residue vector into Z_i and beta_i of that vector equals c_i(z). Then there exists an additive gamma from kappa tensor the product of M_i to the product of H_i whose value on the tensor base change of the product of every admissible b_i is the product of c_i.

source.place: Tag 0BF2, linear algebra of the Picard comparison

proof.text: Choose vector-space complements of the cycle subspaces and project to each cycle subspace. Compose these projections with tensorized coordinate projections and with beta_i, then take their product. Base change respects composition, so each admissible image has the stated coordinate cycle. Each projection fixes that cycle, and the assumed coordinate comparisons yield the product identity. Empty families give equality of the unique empty functions.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BF2, elementary vector-space projections; Mathlib Submodule.exists_isCompl, projectionOnto and LinearMap.baseChange_comp
